beats.t: As the ferry reached midriver, Yeoni opened their palm again. Dawn wind passed between five fingers. The hand still didn't feel like their own.
You should rest, too. You've been holding yourself up on that hurt paw.
Yeongnyangi stumbled as he tried to move. Instinctively, Yeoni supported his little paw. 庚 at their wrist grew warm.
Wait. Don't let go of my hand.

Light spread through every tip of Yeongnyangi's white fur, wrapping his small body. The four marks beneath his hat lit in turn, then sank toward his wrist. The little paw in Yeoni's hand slowly lengthened, beginning at its pink pad.
[ 庚 · Connection restored / Guardian's form restored / Name seal maintained ]
When the light cleared, a silver-haired man sat on the boat's floor. The small navy cloak had lengthened into a silver coat embroidered with gold thread. Yeoni now held a human hand.
...Yeongnyangi?
Yes, it's me. In this form, call me Neo. It's not my real name, but someone called me that a long time ago.
He flexed his fingers. The rust-colored marks remained on his left hand. Only his form had returned. The name hidden for so long was still blocked inside his mouth.
Your hand is warm. Does it still hurt?
A little. Becoming human doesn't heal everything.
Yeoni made room. Neo bent unfamiliar knees and sat. For the first time, their shoulders touched at the same height.
Then let's get used to it slowly. I only just came back, too.
All right. Help me this time.
Moka woke late and looked from one to the other. He opened his mouth, then closed it and draped a blanket over Neo.
Explain after breakfast. You're both shaking.
When Yeoni smiled, Neo smiled faintly, too. His face was unfamiliar, but the habit of looking away when flustered was the same. Only then did Yeoni loosen their grip on his hand.
The boat traveled downriver through the night. Around dawn, a familiar dock appeared. The island that sold time. The smell of baking bread drifted from the end of an alley.
Sis! Sis, come quick! Customers! No, not customers!
Luna!
Huh? Who are you? You sound like Pig Sis, but your face is human.
It's Pig Sis. Now Human Sis.
Wow! Really human! Fingers, too! You can pick up bread!
Luna took Yeoni's hand and shook it up and down, touching each finger in wonder.
Luna, finish with the dough before you play. Oh, our guests.
Luna's sister emerged with flour on her apron. She looked over the group one by one, then smiled like a sigh.
Mr. Cat is human, too? Surprises later. Injuries first. Neo's arm, the fortune-teller's arm, and even the otter's tail.
May I keep calling you Mr. Cat? I'm used to it. Whatever your form, a guest is a guest.
My tail always looks like this!
Everyone inside. Wash, sit, eat. In that order.
The bakery was warm. Fresh bread filled the shelves with steam. The wall clock now moved at its own pace.
Today's first batch. No charge. But you have to eat it all.
Ah. The smell. It's all there. A smell with flavor.
You can eat with your hands now. Slowly. It's hot.
I know. But it smells so good, I can hardly wait.
Yeoni bit into the bread and stopped. It was warm. Butter had melted inside. Sweetness slowly spread over their tongue.
It's good.
Are you crying? Was it too hot?
I don't know. I thought the ledger took everything. But delicious things are still delicious.
Without a word, Luna's sister placed another roll before Yeoni. They ate that, too. And kept crying as they ate. Nobody laughed.
It can take your fortune, but not your appetite. That belongs to your body.
With that, Luna's sister returned to the oven. Her back was a little more stooped than before. Not all the time she had sold had returned.
Miss, may I ask your birth date and time? With bread this good, your Eating God energy must be excellent.
Fortune-teller, keep your mouth shut while eating bread. House rules.
Yes. I like rules.
That's a rule I can get behind.

As the others left the table one by one, full, Yeoni took a bag of bread and sat on the back steps. Neo sat beside them, pulling down his left sleeve. Rust-colored stains remained on the back of his hand.
Don't hide it. I've seen it all now.
Neo hesitated, then rolled up his sleeve. The rust stopped below his shoulder. A changed form hadn't erased the wounds.
I take back telling you to step aside. That's what I went to the river to say.
I know. I heard.
You heard? Where?
Downstream. Even the part about giving me five stars.
Why do you remember that?
I'll promise, too. From now on, I'll say when it hurts. No hiding.
A promise. Customer Support loses stars for breaking promises.
I will. And don't put out your fire. Let's hold on together until the Water thaws.
Yeoni tore off a piece of bread and fed it to Neo. He didn't refuse. For a while, the two chewed in silence.
Back inside, Luna was already racing around with dough for the next batch.
The sun rose a little higher. Carrying a plate of bread, Yeoni went to the window. The alley was still quiet. A few cats drawn by the smell dozed atop a wall.
Across the alley, under the eaves' shadow, sat a black shape. A torn cloak. A golden ring on its right forepaw.
(The tiger.)
The tiger wasn't looking at the bakery. It was pretending not to. Only the tip of its nose tilted ever so slightly toward the bread.
Yeoni started to open the window, then stopped. If they went outside, the tiger would leave. That much seemed certain.
What are you looking at?
Oh, nothing. Just someone outside.
Luna's sister glanced through the window. Without a word, she wrapped a fresh roll in paper and went out.
The alley was cooler than the bakery. As Luna's sister approached the eaves, the tiger rose. Water dripped from its cloak.
I'm only passing through.
Of course. Passing through hungry.
Luna's sister offered the bread. The tiger looked at it, then at her face. Calculating eyes. What was being bought, for how much, and when it must be repaid.
How much is this?
Free.
Nothing is free.
Something is. One thing, right here.
The tiger didn't reach out. Luna's sister didn't wait. She took its paw, opened it, placed the bread on it, and folded it closed again so the bread wouldn't fall.
Eat it warm. Once it cools, it's just bread.
She turned and went back inside. Not once did she look back.
The tiger stood there a long time. The bread in its paw was warm. The golden ring stayed still, as though it had briefly forgotten how to tighten.
Free.
The tiger did not eat the bread. It carefully tucked it inside the torn cloak, beside the place holding the drum boy's name. Then it vanished into shadow.
Back in the bakery, Luna's sister resumed kneading as though nothing had happened.
Thank you.
For what? A bakery is a place that gives people bread.
Yeoni added nothing. The space under the eaves was empty. Only a damp patch remained.
Then light seeped from an old door at the back of the bakery, leading to storage. At first, it looked like oven light. But it spread along every crack like golden thread.
Sis! The storage door's glowing! Another time thief?
That door never opens.
The old door's grain changed into an image on a card. Stars engraved its border, and an open doorway appeared at its center. Below it, words rose instead of a number.
[ THE DOOR · Destiny code 8/8 confirmed · Return available ]
This. I know this. The card from the app at the beginning. I tapped it and came here.
The door home. Only someone with all eight characters can pass.
Then I can go? Home? To my room?
Yes. Your room. The one with the upturned umbrella.
Yeoni took a step toward the door, then stopped and looked back. Moka, Yundal, Luna, Luna's sister. And Neo.
We're all going together, right?
No one answered immediately. Yundal gently held his gloved hand before the door. The golden threads broke off in front of it.
[ Year □□ · Month □□ · Day □□ · Hour ■■ · 7/8 · Entry denied ]
As expected. Not me. I have no birth hour.
Your hour? The one Blue Rabbit ate?
Yes. According to this door, someone missing one of the eight characters isn't quite a complete person yet. A little hurtful.
Then we find it. Together. And afterward, we leave together.
You're willing to wait for me, my lady. Proof we're compatible.
No.
Yundal smiled. But the smile took a little longer to end.
I'm not going, either.
Moka?
I'm an otter from here. Someone has to guard the fire on the festival island. Bring a skewer-grilling otter to the human world, and you'll make the news.
But still.
Still what? One fewer person to hear my rap. That's the only thing I'll miss.
Don't cry, human. You're uglier than you were as a pig.
As he said it, Moka pressed his forehead once against the back of Yeoni's hand. Just as on the day he shared his breath.
Then Neo...
I'm going.
You are?
I'm a borrowed slot. If the slot goes, I follow. And Customer Support makes house calls.
How many stars for the house-call service?
Five. Didn't you say so at the river earlier?
You heard that?
Yeoni and Neo stood before the door. Luna pressed a bag of bread into Yeoni's arms. Her sister merely waved from the oven.
Come back, Sis. Human Sis or Pig Sis, I like both. Come back for sure.
I will. Next time, I'll bring bread. Paid for with money.
If it's not as good as ours, we won't accept it.
My lady. Once you're over there, things here may blur like a dream. But don't worry too much.
They won't blur. How could I forget bread this good?
Of course. You can't forget bread.
Yundal slipped his gloved hand into his pocket. He knew better than anyone what it felt like to be the one forgotten.
Yeoni grasped the handle. Not cold. Warm as fresh bread. The door opened, and a golden wind poured in.
Crossing the threshold, Yeoni thought they heard something behind them. Yundal murmuring very softly, a name other than his own. But the wind covered it.
The door closed. Those left in the bakery watched it for a while. It was an old storage door again.
And where nobody saw, a few raindrops seeped through its closed cracks. To the other side. As though following someone.
